Next Thursday, the Senate Commerce Committee will mark up S. 2817. >>> [CHECK: the memo says “Next Thursday” but dates the markup as Thursday, October 15; from October 8, that is one week away, so the date is consistent, but the current date context is 2026.]
“the stakes for our coverage has never been higher” >>> “the stakes for our coverage have never been higher”
“federal goverment's” >>> “federal government's”
“more then ever” >>> “more than ever”
“it's definitions” >>> “its definitions”
“central principal” >>> “central principle”
“enforcment regime” >>> “enforcement regime”
“directly effect every company” >>> “directly affect every company”
“Senator Whitfield (R-OK)” >>> “Senator Whitfield (R-OH)” [CHECK: the memo gives two different states for Whitfield.]
“narrows the registry in Section 5” >>> “narrows the registry in Section 4” [CHECK: the bill summary places the registry in Section 4, not Section 5.]
“keeps the $10 million daily civil penalty in Section 5” >>> “keeps the $10 million daily civil penalty in Section 5” [CHECK: the bill summary says Section 5 sets penalties of up to $1 million per day, not $10 million.]
“who's support” >>> “whose support”
“the amendment's changes is modest” >>> “the amendment's changes are modest”
“Gallager” >>> “Gallagher” [CHECK: confirm spelling.]
“of the committees 28 members” >>> “of the committee's 28 members”
“13 are yes or leaning yes, 10 are no or leaning no, and 6 are undecided” >>> “13 are yes or leaning yes, 10 are no or leaning no, and 5 are undecided” [CHECK: the listed totals add to 29, while the memo says there are 28 members; the five named undecided senators also conflict with the stated six.]
“Senator Chen, Ellis, Alvarez, Pike, and Barlow” >>> “Senators Chen, Ellis, Alvarez, Pike, and Barlow”
“before the markup on Thursday, October 14” >>> “before the markup on Thursday, October 15” [CHECK: October 14, 2026, is Wednesday.]
“in a seperate interview” >>> “in a separate interview”
“the list ... are attached” >>> “the list ... is attached”
“Commerce Commitee markup” >>> “Commerce Committee markup”
“the week November 16” >>> “the week of November 16”
“occured” >>> “occurred”
“a close compliment to S. 2817” >>> “a close complement to S. 2817”
“with the the offices” >>> “with the offices”
“there senators” >>> “their senators”
“you should recieve” >>> “you should receive”
“six Hill reporters” >>> “five Hill reporters” [CHECK: the memo gives conflicting counts for the Hill reporting team.]
